references.title: Nebraska, USA — Google Data Center Location

patch.longFormSummary:
• Google’s timeline also describes the Omaha announcement in 2022. January 1, 2022 is a year-only construction/announcement marker, not a precise first-service date.
  • The prior chip counts, H100 equivalents, five generators, 700 sqft and daily water reading have no matched primary campus evidence and are removed with the dependent calculated energy.
  • Timeline: This pin now identifies the known Omaha campus and published 2022 milestone. A separately dated 2028 expansion needs its own primary phase evidence.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Operator says Omaha built in 2022 and lists its announcement in that year. Year placeholder, not an exact operating date.

gaps: Resolve build versus first-service milestone and exact date; verify any independently announced 2028 expansion, site budget and hardware.

patch.title: Meta Aiken: $800M+ Campus; Spring 2027 Target and Closed-Loop Cooling
patch.description: Meta’s current fact sheet gives an $800 million-plus Aiken investment and closed-loop liquid cooling. South Carolina’s announcement describes a 715,000-square-foot Sage Mill campus expected operational in spring 2027. The former $1.2B / 91 MW scope is removed.

references.title: Meta Aiken Data Center — Information Sheet
Meta selects Aiken County for first South Carolina data center

patch.longFormSummary:
• The cooling system is designed for no operational cooling water according to Meta. That does not establish zero total site water demand; Breezy Hill provides water and wastewater service.
  • The 137 MW of renewable projects described by Meta is off-site clean-energy addition, not published campus IT demand. The prior 450-acre area and capacity-scaled consumption lack support.
  • Timeline: April 1, 2027 is a seasonal placeholder for the state’s announced spring 2027 target, not a published exact opening day.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: State announcement says spring 2027; April 1 is a seasonal estimate, not an exact COD.

datacenter.cooling: Planned closed-loop liquid cooling; Meta states zero operational cooling water
datacenter.note: 715,000 sqft is initial campus scope from SC Commerce. No total daily site water reading is published; zero refers to the cooling-system design.

gaps: Verify current spring-2027 schedule, total site water demand, exact parcel, phases and utility/IT capacity.
Existing primary-source campus pin7307 overlaps this record; queue consolidation preserving authors and attachments.

patch.title: Meta Los Lunas: Official Budget Identifies $800M 2025 Expansion
patch.description: The Village of Los Lunas FY2026 budget identifies Meta’s third data-center expansion as an $800 million direct investment in 2025. Meta’s current U.S. fleet page gives $2.5 billion-plus for the entire campus, a different scope from this expansion.

references.title: Village of Los Lunas — FY2026 Final Budget, page 15
Meta — U.S. Data Center Fleet

patch.longFormSummary:
• The official budget’s printed page 15 distinguishes the 2025 expansion from cumulative community investment. It replaces the unsupported $1B expansion price.
  • Neither source supports the pin’s 99 MW expansion load, 700 acres or 118,630 gallons/day. Unsupported area/cooling/water claims and dependent annual energy are removed.
  • Timeline: June 1, 2027 remains an unverified legacy commissioning estimate. The budget establishes the 2025 investment announcement, not first service; an expansion-specific schedule is still needed.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy June 2027 COD; official budget verifies a 2025 expansion investment, not commissioning.

gaps: Obtain expansion-specific operator/contractor RFS date, building scope, exact parcel, IT/utility capacity and water permit; do not reuse whole-campus figures.

patch.title: Meta Montgomery: $1.5B+ Investment; Capacity and Opening Date Unpublished
patch.description: Meta’s current Montgomery fact sheet publishes a $1.5 billion-plus investment. It supersedes the initial $800M-plus announcement. The source does not establish the old 106 MW load, 380-acre site or June 2027 commissioning date.

references.title: Meta Montgomery Data Center — Information Sheet
Hello, Montgomery!

patch.longFormSummary:
• The current fact sheet identifies Alabama Power and Montgomery Water Works and describes efficient cooling without a published daily water volume or a specified evaporative design.
  • The initial announcement described 715,000 sqft; it is historical initial scope, not assumed to represent the larger current investment. Prior estimated daily water and calculated annual energy are cleared.
  • Timeline: June 1, 2027 remains an unverified legacy date. The current fact sheet gives no precise commissioning date, so it stays estimated.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy June 2027 COD; current operator fact sheet does not publish an exact first-service date.

datacenter.cooling: Water-efficient cooling planned; specific technology unpublished in current fact sheet
datacenter.note: No verified daily water or 380-acre area. Historic initial 715,000 sqft scope is not asserted as the current expanded campus total.

gaps: Obtain latest phase area, schedule, exact parcel, campus power and water/cooling specifications.
Existing primary-source campus pin7290 overlaps this record; queue consolidation preserving authors and attachments.

patch.title: Terra San Jose: Planned Fuel-Cell Campus at 4701 North First Street
patch.description: Arcadis describes Terra Ventures’ planned San Jose campus with a 295,080-square-foot data-center/power structure and a separate 131,903-square-foot power structure. CPUC’s November 2025 environmental record places Terra at 4701 North First Street, San Jose, correcting the former Santa Clara city location.

references.title: Near-net-zero data center campus in San Jose — Arcadis
Power the South Bay — Final EIR Comments and Responses, page 7-223

patch.longFormSummary:
• The Phase 1 total is 426,983 sqft including the power structures. The design uses natural-gas fuel cells, with waste heat driving absorption chillers; backup generators are eliminated in the design. These are plans, not measured operation.
  • The map point is street-address interpolation at approximately 37.42247, -121.96475, not a surveyed parcel boundary. The old $850M, 99 MW and 12 acres are unverified and cleared.
  • Timeline: June 1, 2029 remains an unverified legacy COD marker. Neither designer nor CPUC record confirms commissioning.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy June 2029 COD; opened primary design and environmental sources do not publish commissioning.
patch.address: 4701 North First Street, San Jose (Alviso), California, USA

datacenter.note: Phase 1 total includes 295080 sqft DC/attached power structure plus131903 sqft standalone power structure. No verified IT MW, acreage or daily water consumption.

gaps: Verify current permit/schedule, campus power, water and exact surveyed parcel; ArcGIS point is approximate street interpolation.

patch.title: Gravitas I Solar: 1,124.75 MW ERCOT Request, No IA; Target June 2030
patch.description: ERCOT’s September 2026 report lists Gravitas I Solar (30INR0083), S&S Renewables LLC, in Pecos County at 1,124.75 MW, with projected COD June 30, 2030 and no interconnection agreement. The prior $1.3B cost is unsupported.

references.title: ERCOT GIS Report — September 2026

patch.longFormSummary:
• Project Details – Large Gen row 1745 is the solar request. Other similarly named gas or wind requests are separate and must not be combined.
  • Timeline: June 30, 2030 is a queue target, not confirmed operation. The prior tax-agreement URL was not proven to identify this exact project; queue references replace it.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: ERCOT September 2026 GIS row1745 projected COD; no IA, estimated.

power.note: Queue30INR0083 solar equipment request; no executed IA.

gaps: Verify exact project-specific tax/permit record, developer relationship, construction budget and parcel; track IA progress.

patch.title: Copia Stanley: La Paz Approves 500 MW PV/BESS Permit; Operator Lists Larger Scope
patch.description: La Paz County approved Stanley’s conditional-use permit on January 5, 2026. Minutes describe approximately 3,962 acres and a 500 MW photovoltaic-and-battery facility. Copia’s portfolio lists 1,000 MW PV and 1,000 MW storage; these scopes remain unreconciled.

references.title: La Paz County Board of Supervisors — January 5, 2026 Minutes
Stanley — Copia Power
BLM National PLSS CadNSDI — T3N R12W Sections 19–22 and 24–29

patch.longFormSummary:
• The county record identifies Copia and eastern La Paz County near I-10, north of the CAP Canal. The permit’s 500 MW description does not provide a separate battery discharge rating. The former $1.9B is cleared.
  • Location is the approximate center of the extent of ten named PLSS sections, derived from BLM geometry: 33.58061, -113.49076. These sections encompass more than the actual project footprint; the point is not a surveyed boundary.
  • Timeline: January 5, 2026 is the verified CUP approval event, replacing the unverified December 2029 opening. Neither source confirms COD. County permit scope and larger operator portfolio are shown separately, not equated to queue2331.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed date of county CUP approval, not commercial operation.
patch.address: T3N R12W, I-10 corridor near Cielo Azul, eastern La Paz County, Arizona, USA (approximate PLSS section-area center)

power.note: County-described500MW PV/BESS permit; not separate battery MW or measured generation.
